world.h: US and Iran both claim control of Hormuz
world.b: Washington and Tehran each say they control the Strait of Hormuz amid attacks on vessels. UK maritime monitor UKMTO says it is struggling to count attacks because most targeted ships refuse to report them.
world.title: US and Iran both claim control of Strait of Hormuz amid attacks on vessels

world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage: Iran's Revolutionary Guard warns the Strait of Hormuz is 'closed' as four tankers are reported hit.
world.title: Iran’s IRGC warns Strait of Hormuz is ‘closed’ as 4 tankers reported hit

national.h: No Kings shifts focus to early voting
national.b: Grassroots groups plan more than 3,000 "No Kings: Vote Early" marches and events Saturday to help people register and plan their ballots.
national.title: No Kings turns its focus to voting this weekend. Here's what we know

national.h: Teen gunman kills 4 at Oregon elementary school
national.b: A 16-year-old shot his way into Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, killing three children and a teacher, before being shot by a person who followed him inside, police said.

politics.h: Congress outraged as Trump waives Russia sanctions
politics.b: Lawmakers in both parties criticized Trump's order pausing sanctions on the Russian economy, with Sen. Thom Tillis calling it 'beyond irresponsible,' but no quick counter is expected. Zelenskyy urged support for the sanctions.
politics.title: Trump's decision to waive Russian sanctions outrages Congress, but no quick counter seen

politics.h: Speaker Johnson draws on faith to hold House
politics.b: House Speaker Mike Johnson is leaning on his recruits, his fundraising for House Republicans and his faith as he fights to keep the GOP majority. 'We run to win, and that's biblical,' he said in Maine.
politics.title: House Speaker Mike Johnson draws on faith as he fights to hold the Republican majority

politics.h: Trump vowed swing-district blitz, visits red states
politics.b: Trump pledged to campaign in 35 competitive races but has campaigned with fewer than a third of those candidates.
politics.title: Trump promised a swing district blitz. He's going to a lot of very red states

politics.h: DOJ warns California officials on ballots
politics.b: A Justice Department letter says officials who process mail ballots from suspected noncitizens risk prosecution, a day after the administration sued the state.
politics.title: DOJ says California officials who process ballots from suspected noncitizens risk prosecution

politics.b: A Joint Economic Committee minority report says Trump's pharma holdings rose to as much as $56.2 million, including up to $39.1 million in firms that got Medicare negotiation exemptions.

politics.h: Press secretary Zacharia out after five days
politics.b: The White House says Katie Zacharia is "transitioning out." Trump had told her to "reconsider" staying and said there was no rush to name a replacement.
The president is visiting battleground Georgia to boost GOP enthusiasm despite party divisions in the state.

politics.h: Talarico casts Texas Senate race as David vs. Goliath
politics.b: The Democrat told supporters "you are my slingshot" after Republicans invested more than $158 million against him.

politics.h: Court weighs who owns the president's papers
politics.b: Administration lawyers argue before a federal appeals court Friday that White House papers belong to Donald Trump, not the public, after the Justice Department moved to invalidate the Presidential Records Act.

international.h: Masked settlers attack European diplomats
international.b: Settlers in the West Bank village of Taybeh targeted Belgium's consul general, French and Polish diplomats and Catholic representatives, Belgium's foreign minister said. A French mayor was assaulted and a Belgian vehicle damaged.
international.title: Masked settlers attack European diplomats in the occupied West Bank

international.h: Biggest protest in years against Tunisia's Saied
international.b: Thousands marched against President Kais Saied, backed by the UGTT trade union federation, opposition parties and civil society groups. AFP put the crowd at more than 3,000.
international.title: Thousands rally for biggest protest in years against Tunisia’s Saied

international.h: Pope Leo returns to Vatican after surgery
international.b: Pope Leo, 71, left hospital four days after having the lower lobe of his right lung removed. His surgeon said there is no clinical reason he cannot make his Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Peru and Argentina.
international.title: Pope returns to Vatican days after surgery; surgeon says he should be fit for Latin America tour

international.h: Protesters clash with police across France
international.b: Riot police used tear gas against hooded, masked protesters in Paris as nationwide demonstrations spread, with dozens reportedly detained around Place de la Republique. In Marseille, local media said protesters breached the town hall.
international.title: Tens of thousands protest for reforms in France amid tear gas and unrest

international.h: Settlers injure child, four women in West Bank
international.b: Israeli settlers attacked residents of Ma'in village in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron, injuring six people including four women and a child, the Palestine Red Crescent said. Elsewhere, Israeli forces fired on olive-picking farmers near Ramallah, Wafa reported.
international.title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats during West Bank olive harvest

international.h: Israeli rabbi's olive ruling sparks uproar
international.b: Prominent rabbi Dov Lior issued a religious ruling permitting settlers to take olives from Palestinian orchards in the occupied West Bank, arguing landowners blocked from their harvests had been 'compensated' in earlier years.
international.title: Hardline Israeli rabbi ruling on stolen Palestinian olives prompts uproar

international.h: Egypt's Sisi offers defence help to Saudi Arabia
international.b: Speaking at an Egyptian Military Academy graduation, President el-Sisi said Egypt is ready to 'carry out any measure to protect' Saudi Arabia if Riyadh asks, and is seeking authorisation for defence assistance.
international.title: Egypt’s Sisi seeks authorisation for defence assistance to Saudi Arabia

international.h: Solar booms in Philippines as Iran war lifts power bills
international.b: Electricity prices have soared since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February, pushing a growing number of Filipino households to install rooftop solar panels to cut their bills.

international.h: South Africans seek justice for apartheid crimes
international.b: Decades after apartheid ended, families of victims, including those killed when police opened fire on protesters on March 21, 1960, are still pressing for accountability in a neglected township near Johannesburg.
international.title: Decades after apartheid, South Africans seek justice for crimes of the past

international.h: Russian attacks kill 8, cut power to 1 million
international.b: Strikes on nine Ukrainian regions hit two shopping centres. In Kharkiv, two people were killed and 12 wounded, the governor said.

international.h: Sudan army claims strikes on RSF in Nyala
international.b: The army says dozens of RSF fighters were killed in South Darfur. The RSF says a drone hit a livestock market, killing 30 civilians.

international.h: IMF urges help for poorer nations hit by war
international.b: Kristalina Georgieva said as annual meetings ended in Bangkok that low-income countries face rising debt, high inflation and war spillovers.

international.h: Israel's opposition unites against Netanyahu
international.b: Yair Lapid, Naftali Bennett, Gadi Eisenkot, Yair Golan and Avigdor Liberman met in Tel Aviv and published shared principles ahead of the Oct. 27 election.

international.h: Three jailed 158 years for killing surfers
international.b: A judge in Ensenada sentenced three men for the 2024 murders of Australian brothers Callum and Jake Robinson and their American friend Jack Carter Rhoad.

international.h: US Coast Guard rescues 16 after boat sinks off Baja
international.b: The boat went down about 140 miles west of Ensenada. A search continues for 11 people believed missing.

international.h: Cameroonians await reshuffle after Biya's return
international.b: President Paul Biya, 93, returned in August after about 10 weeks abroad, but no new government has been named and the vice presidency remains vacant.

international.h: Carney: outsiders "working to break" Canada
international.b: At a Calgary rally, the prime minister warned against Alberta's vote on whether to start a path toward a separation referendum.

international.h: Russia strikes 9 Ukrainian regions
international.b: The attacks came amid fears that strained ties between Kyiv and Washington leave Ukraine more exposed to aerial assaults on its power grid before winter.

international.h: Kenya records third Ebola case
international.b: A 65-year-old woman, a close relative of the first two cases, tested positive after being quarantined since Oct. 6, the Health Ministry said.

international.h: Pope Leo to appear in public Sunday
international.b: The 71-year-old pope, who had part of his right lung removed Tuesday, can now carry out daily activities independently, his doctors said.

international.h: Settlers attack olive pickers, US journalist
international.b: Israeli settlers beat Palestinian olive pickers and a Washington Post photojournalist in the occupied West Bank and set olive groves ablaze.

international.h: Gaza starvation at 'catastrophic' levels
international.b: At least 466 Palestinians have died of malnutrition and starvation since 2024, a third of them children, the Gaza Health Ministry said on World Food Day.

international.h: EU leaders rally behind Ukraine
international.b: At a Brussels summit attended by Zelenskyy, top EU officials stressed keeping up arms for Ukraine and sanctions on Russia. "This is no time to withdraw support," said Antonio Costa.

international.h: Pakistan orders school checks after roof collapse
international.b: At least 34 students aged 13 or younger and a teacher were killed when a roof collapsed at Al-Khair school in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

international.h: Ethiopia installs interim government in Tigray
international.b: The move follows the military pushing back an uprising the TPLF launched last month. Free elections were pledged to follow.

international.h: Croatia leaders condemn pro-Nazi chants
international.b: Hajduk Split fans marched through Split chanting pro-Nazi and antisemitic slogans before Thursday's match against Ajax.

international.h: China tells Israel to stop West Bank settlements
international.b: Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Israeli President Isaac Herzog that Israel should stop and reverse its "forced establishment" of settlements, China's foreign ministry said.

international.h: Argentine students protest Milei cuts
international.b: Students at the University of Buenos Aires covered a faculty hall with banners against President Javier Milei's spending cuts and called an assembly to announce an occupation.

international.h: Iraq parliament completes al-Zaidi's cabinet
international.b: Lawmakers approved 11 remaining portfolios and three deputy prime ministers, one of them under US sanctions, completing Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's government.

international.h: Drone strike on tanker in Romanian waters
international.b: A drone hit the chemical tanker Wine Trader about 13 nautical miles off Sulina. Five people were rescued and seven are missing. President Nicusor Dan promised "a reaction from the Romanian state."

international.h: Saudi says Iran is encouraging Houthi attacks
international.b: Saudi diplomat Rayed Krimly said Iran is encouraging the Houthi escalation. At least 19 people have been killed in more than a week of attacks, and Riyadh's King Khalid airport has been targeted 20 times this month.

international.h: Harry and Meghan make first joint UK appearances
international.b: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex visited a youth recording studio and a food bank in Nottingham, their first joint appearances since returning to the UK.

international.h: Myanmar's leader wins back neighbours
international.b: Min Aung Hlaing, whose 2021 power grab triggered a civil war, received a red-carpet welcome with an honour guard in Kuala Lumpur last week.

international.h: Sally Rooney's books pulled from UK sale
international.b: Publisher Faber said UK law bars it from passing on earnings to Rooney, who pledged them to a group the UK designates as a terrorist organization.

business.h: China to curb tech exports, including AI
business.b: The commerce ministry listed 23 AI technologies, from large models to agents, for export bans or restrictions, citing national security.

business.h: AI borrowing slows as debt jitters hit tech
business.b: Morgan Stanley data show debt issuance for AI projects slowed last month from a June record, and CoreWeave bonds fell sharply as stocks slumped on borrowing-cost fears.

science.h: Nature funding falls short before UN summit
science.b: Countries are behind on raising $200 billion a year for biodiversity as the COP17 talks open Monday to review the 2022 "30x30" targets.
science.title: Fundraising to protect key natural sites falls short ahead of UN biodiversity summit

science.b: ACOG updated its guidelines for the first time since 2014, recommending hormone therapy alongside antidepressants and nonhormonal options for symptoms like hot flashes and insomnia.

sports.h: Southern Nazarene's Tyler Ulrich dies at 21
sports.b: The sophomore defensive player died after five days in hospital following an injury in last week's game at Ouachita Baptist. Saturday's game against Southwestern Oklahoma State was canceled.
sports.title: College football player dies: Southern Nazarene's Tyler Ulrich, 21, was injured in game last week

sports.b: Wil Lutz's field goal won it after a Sam Darnold interception. Analyst Ryan Fitzpatrick ripped Bo Nix, who threw for 107 yards.

sports.h: Brewers sweep Dodgers, reach World Series
sports.b: Milwaukee won Game 4 6-4 to complete the NLCS sweep. Jake Bauers, with six RBI in the series, was named NLCS MVP.
FIFA president Gianni Infantino apologized over this year's World Cup controversies, but European delegates said "no satisfactory answers were provided."

sports.h: Caleb Williams pushes back on injury reports
sports.b: The Bears quarterback is on track for a possible Week 6 return from his hamstring injury but said he still doesn't know if he'll play Sunday against Atlanta.

sports.h: Josh Jacobs sues to block release of video
sports.b: The Packers running back filed suit against a Wisconsin police department to keep evidence from his criminal case, including an alleged video, from being released.

sports.h: Eagles rule out Jalen Hurts with blood clot
sports.b: A follow-up ultrasound found movement in a blood clot in Hurts' calf, so he will miss Sunday's game against Carolina.

goodnews.b: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower near Central Park, the first documented barn owl nest in Manhattan in modern history, drawing nightly crowds.

local.h: Man shot near Midtown subway station
local.b: A man was shot Saturday afternoon near the 53rd Street and 7th Avenue station, which serves the B, D and E lines, the NYPD said. Police released no other details, and his condition was unclear.
local.title: Man shot near Midtown subway station Saturday afternoon, NYPD says

local.h: NYPD seeks Yorkie dognapped in Queens
local.b: Chanel, a 10-year-old Yorkshire Terrier, was taken from her front lawn in College Point late last month when two people in a Subaru Forester scooped her up and sped off, police said.
local.title: Have you seen this Yorkie? NYPD looking for adorable pup dognapped from her Queens home

local.h: Knicks fans adjust to life as champions
local.b: After winning the 2026 NBA Championship, the Knicks will raise their first championship banner at Madison Square Garden in 50 years as they open their season.
local.title: Being reigning champions is weird for Knicks fans, but we could get used to this.

local.h: Tompkins Square Park makeover splits regulars
local.b: A community board committee backed renovating the basketball courts, kids' pool and 1990s outdoor fitness area. Some park users say it goes too far.
local.title: Tompkins Square Park is getting a makeover. Some say it's too much.

local.h: Pfizer Building fix: 1/64th of an inch at a time
local.b: Engineering plans for the city's largest office-to-housing conversion show crews will jack sagging floors up about 7 inches in tiny increments.
local.title: Inside the plan to fix the nearly collapsed Pfizer Building, 1/64th of an inch at a time

local.h: Storms, wind and chill hit NYC weather
local.b: Temperatures drop from near 80 Thursday to the 50s by Saturday, with potentially dangerous storms Friday evening, the NWS says.
local.title: NYC’s whiplash weather continues into weekend with heavy winds, chilly temps, NWS says

local.h: Mamdani urges parking lots to ban ICE
local.b: The mayor and more than 100 elected officials asked lot and garage owners not to make their property available to ICE as a staging ground.
local.title: Mamdani and 100+ NY officials urge parking lot owners to ban ICE

local.b: A city comptroller's report found EMS teams are taking longer to reach people even as life-threatening emergencies rise.
local.title: NYC ambulance response times have grown 41% as life-threatening calls rise

local.h: Judge tosses Trump suit over NYC sanctuary laws
local.b: A federal judge dismissed the administration's lawsuit challenging the city's limits on cooperating with immigration authorities.
local.title: Federal judge tosses Trump administration lawsuit challenging NYC sanctuary laws

local.b: Police charged Francis Cabello, 32, with murder in the death of her daughter Fabiana in Richmond Hill, a day after she called 911.
local.title: Death of Queens girl may be due to asphyxia, DA says

periods.name: This Afternoon
periods.text: Partly sunny, with a high near 54. North wind around 16 mph, with gusts as high as 28 mph.

periods.name: Tonight
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 40. North wind 11 to 14 mph.

periods.name: Sunday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 55. Northeast wind 6 to 9 mph.

periods.name: Sunday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 46. Northeast wind 3 to 7 mph.

periods.name: Monday
periods.text: Mostly sunny, with a high near 61. Northeast wind around 10 mph.

periods.name: Monday Night
periods.text: Mostly cloudy, with a low around 52.
